results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run alongside them.

Bringer of the Last Gift has no recent lists at all, and Superior Spider-Man appears in only one. Town Greeter is mostly in Golgari Roots. Next I'll check the field and the two shells that use these cards.

Golgari Roots and Rogue are both built around mill and graveyard plays, which fits the requested cards. Next I'll find the mill, self-surveil and graveyard enablers that are legal in Standard.

The field is aggro-heavy, so a slow mill deck has to be efficient. I'll check the mill and graveyard cards from the menu, plus the blue sources I'd need to splash for Superior Spider-Man.

The mill and recursion pieces are clear now. Before I fix the removal suite, I need to confirm which black and green removal is legal, and check a few graveyard payoffs.

I have enough to build. The chosen direction is Golgari with a light blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. I'll run the checker against the Golgari Roots mana base first.

The checker flags the mana base: 17 lands is light for an 8-drop finisher. I'll move to 18 lands and cut one Scavenging Ooze, which would otherwise exile the creature cards my reanimation needs.

Only the ramp-count warning remains, and I'll justify it in the write-up. Next I'll check the odds that matter most: finding a blue source for the splash, and finding Superior Spider-Man.

Blue sources come up by turn 5 in 72% of games, and Spider-Man plus a blue source by turn 7 in about 30%. That's a real but modest splash, and I'll say so. The build passes the checker with no errors, so I'll submit it.

The checker flagged three cards as rarely played. Each one does a specific job in this plan, so I'll keep them and explain why.

I built a Golgari mill deck with a light blue splash for Superior Spider-Man, borrowing the Golgari Roots shell (Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk, the mill package and its mana). The plan is to fill both graveyards early with Town Greeter, Dredger's Insight and Overlord, copy the best creature with Spider-Man (a milled Bringer makes a 6/6 flyer for 4), then cast Bringer on turn 8 to sacrifice the board and return every creature from both graveyards. The deck was accepted with 18 lands plus Llanowar Elves and Molt Tender for the 8-drop.

I picked this over a Dimir build because Dimir has no real self-mill and no Town Greeter. Mill density is the main reason for Golgari, and Spider-Man's blue is a single splash card. The checker's ramp warning is intentional: four Elves, three Molt Tenders and Town Greeter's land-to-hand supply the mana for Bringer.

The main risks are real. Bringer and Spider-Man have no recent published lists, so this is untested. Blue sources come up by turn 5 in about 72% of games, and Spider-Man plus a blue source by turn 7 in about 30%. The win line (every card drawn by turn 8) shows up in only about 5% of games, so expect this to be a slow, grindy deck against Izzet and Vivi aggro.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run alongside them.

The three requested cards have never appeared together in a published list. I'll check each one's pairings separately and the current Standard field.

The field has a few clear shells. Before choosing a direction, I'll pull the Landfall and Boros reference lists and search for landfall and warp cards in green and red.

The landfall and warp pools in red and green are deep enough for a real shell. Next I'll look up the candidate cards and lands I might use.

Screaming Nemesis shows as banned in Standard, so it stays out. I'll confirm the last few creatures I plan to use, then check the mana.

The mana checks out: 91% to find a green source and 83% for blue by turn 4. Next I'll check the 60-card list and pull sideboard options in red and green.

The check flagged 16 lands as light for a landfall deck, since the reference Landfall list runs about 25. I'll move to 18 lands, trimming a Sazh's Chocobo and Snakeskin Veil, and add a 15-card sideboard aimed at the field: artifacts, Vivi, Reanimator and the burn decks.

The 18-land list passes with no errors. The remaining warning is a generic formula. I'll keep 18 lands because the deck needs land drops for its landfall triggers and has mana sinks, and the four Llanowar Elves and two Traveling Chocobo add mana. Next I'll check how often the key turn-4 cards show up.

Submitting the deck now.

I built a Gruul landfall deck (red-green with a light blue splash) around Mightform Harmonizer and Full Bore, with Spell Snare as a one-copy splash. Harmonizer's warp lets it attack on the turn it comes down: Full Bore gives it haste and trample after a land entering doubles its power. The landfall ramp and payoffs come from the Landfall list, and the burn and Nova Hellkite supply reach and closers.

I weighed three directions: this Gruul landfall shell, a red aggro list with Full Bore and Harmonizer as a lone green splash, and an Izzet tempo list with Spell Snare and Full Bore. I chose the landfall shell because it is the only one where Harmonizer is a real engine, and Harmonizer is the card the deck is built around.

Things you should know:
- No published list runs these three cards together, so this is a brew. Its tested turn-5 line (Harmonizer on turn 4, then Nova Hellkite and burn) is unplayed.
- The line needs all of its cards by turn 5 in only about 2% of games, so expect it to be a plan you assemble over several turns rather than a turn-4 kill.
- Spell Snare only counters mana value 2 spells, so it is the weakest fit. It needs the blue sources (one Island plus eight fetch lands) to show up.
- Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so I left it out even though the Izzet and Boros lists run it heavily.
- The mana checker still warns that 18 lands is light for a deck with this curve. I kept 18 because the deck needs land drops for its triggers and has mana sinks, and four Llanowar Elves help. Going to 17 lands would be a reasonable change if flooding shows up.

The check is clean: no errors or warnings, and the 15 green and 13 white sources cover both colors. The 21-land count matches Selesnya Offense's proven mana with four Llanowar Elves. I'll submit this as a brew that borrows the Selesnya Offense shell.

I built a green-white deck that uses Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa as the core, with the Selesnya Offense creature base (Llanowar Elves, Pawpatch Recruit, Ouroboroid, Innkeeper's Talent). I considered three directions: a green-white Ally-token deck built on the little-played Earth Kingdom cards, this Selesnya pump-plus-airbend build, and a Bramble Familiar Fetch Quest value deck. The plan: ramp with Llanowar Elves and Bramble Familiar, then put Ouroboroid's growing counters on the board. results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built a blue-red Elemental deck around Ashling and Sunderflock, with Bounce Off as cheap interaction. It's a brew, since no published list plays these cards together.

**Direction chosen:** U/R Elementals with Izzet's burn and mana base. I considered a Simic Ouroboroid package, but it has no Elemental synergy, so Sunderflock would stay a 9-mana card. A straight Izzet Aggro list would have left out the Sunderflock payoff.

**The plan:** Ashling comes down on turn 2. On turn 3, paying {U} at the first main phase flips it to Rimebound, which adds 2 mana each turn for spells with mana value 4 or more. That ramps Sunspine Lynx and Eddymurk Crab into the board. With Crab (mana value 7) on the battlefield, Sunderflock costs {U}{U}, and its cast-only trigger returns the opponent's non-Elemental creatures while your Elementals stay. Target win turn is 5, but the full line is only about 1% likely to be assembled by then, so expect it to be a mid-game plan more often than a turn-5 kill.

**Things to know:**
- Ashling is in opening hands by turn 3 about 49% of the time.
- The checker warned that 17 lands is below its 24-land benchmark. I kept 17 because Ashling, Stratosoarer and Ice Flan add mana or land-finding, and the curve is top-heavy.
- Obliterating Bolt got a card note because a cheaper bounce spell is more common in Standard. I kept it as the deck's only 4-damage exile removal.
- Badgermole Cub and Stormchaser's Talent are banned in Standard, so the Simic and Lessons lists in the menu can't be copied as-is.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I built a mono-black control deck around Doomsday Excruciator, with Insatiable Avarice and Archenemy's Charm as support. It's a brew: no published list plays these three together, so the plan is unproven.

**Directions considered:**
1. **Mono-black control (chosen).** Excruciator needs six black pips and Charm needs three, so only a near-mono-black mana base casts them on curve. I borrowed the black base, removal and card-flow cards from the Mono-Black list, which went 5-0 in a recent league.
2. **Dimir Midrange package.** This has the strongest removal and card quality in the meta, but with blue mana Excruciator would rarely be castable. I rejected it.
3. **Reanimator package.** It is black-heavy and uses Overlord of the Balemurk, but it depends on Bringer and Superior Spider-Man, and Excruciator is awkward there. I rejected it.

**The plan:** Removal and Overlord of the Balemurk hold the board while I build toward Doomsday Excruciator. Each player mills down to six cards, and I get an extra card every upkeep off the 6/6 flier. The opponent's mill is symmetric, so I would deck first in a straight race. The real win is Insatiable Avarice's draw-three mode aimed at the opponent, which takes their six cards to three and deks them on their draw step. Archenemy's Charm can exile a blocker or return a dead Excruciator to hand.

**Caveats:**
- The line was drawn by turn 9 in only about 5.6% of games, per the submit tool. Expect a slow, grindy game.
- I ran 19 black sources (18 Swamp, Realm of Koh), below the roughly 24 in Mono-Black lists. Their extra lands include a colorless manland that would hurt BBBBBB, so I left it out. The checker still warns the land count is light.
- Excruciator is a single copy because it is a six-drop with a symmetric mill. Its six black pips will often not be online until turn 8 or later.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros Dwarves-and-Equipment brew around the three cards, and the deck was accepted with 60 cards and a 15-card sideboard.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three: RW Dwarves-Equipment, a Dwarf build in another colour pair, and a Gearhulk/artifact shell. I chose RW because Kíli (W), Dwarven Mauler (R) and Dáin's Company (RW) only meet in those colours, and Boros Aggro's burn and mana base already run well in the last 30 days. Published lists haven't played these three together, so this is a brew, not a proven list.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) aggro brew around the three Eidolon and Mascot cards, and the deck was accepted. It is a brew, not a proven list. It uses Mono-White Aggro's creature and mana base as a shell, with red burn for removal.

**Plan:** Spirit Mascot and Dog Walker, Boros Recruit, Tenth District Legionnaire and Pursue the Past are the multicolored spells. Each one, cast from hand, returns a sacrificed Eidolon to hand, and Mascot grows whenever a card leaves the graveyard. The win line is Sandstorm Eidolon's sacrifice to stop a blocker, then Boros Recruit after combat to return it, with Battle Screech flyers to finish.

**Honest caveats:**
- Pauper has few legal multicolored spells. Lightning Helix, Boros Charm and the other Boros charms are not legal, so the recursion has only 16 enablers. The odds of drawing at least one by turn 6 are about 97%, but the Eidolons are still weak 2/2s without it.
- No published list runs these cards together, so the win line is untested.
- I chose this direction over a W/U or W/B Eidolon build. Those would have only one Eidolon colour and fewer enablers, which made the recursion even thinner.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
**Submitted: a UB Living Death reanimator brew** (60 cards, 15 lands, 6 mana accelerants). It borrows the Reanimator shell from the current 5-0 Premodern list, but swaps that list's green fatties for black and colorless ones so the deck runs one main color pair.

**The plan:** Careful Study on turn 3 discards Visara and Phyrexian Devourer into the graveyard. Withered Wretch clears the opponent's graveyard so Living Death returns none of their creatures. On turn 5, Living Death (3BB, with Dark Ritual or Lotus Petal to help) sacrifices the boards and returns my fatties, and Visara then picks off what they rebuild.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. BG with the list's Multani, Symbiotic Wurm and Verdant Force has bigger bodies, but the GGG costs are heavy and it has no cheap way to discard its own fatties. Mono-black with Mortivore, Chainer and Gravedigger has easier mana, but thinner threats. I picked UB because Careful Study is the only cheap self-discard, and blue gives Mana Leak to protect the five-mana Living Death.

**Honest odds:** Living Death is in hand by turn 5 about 57% of the time on the play. The full win line is drawn by turn 6 only about 3% of the time, so this is a grindy deck that depends on Careful Study early. The checker flagged 15 lands against a suggested count near 22; I kept 15 because the six accelerants plus Careful Study keep the curve workable.
